description: Phase 6ab gate — INSERT OR IGNORE and INSERT OR REPLACE conflict-resolution. Reuses 9g UNIQUE-probe + existing DeleteRow/InsertRow machinery. No new opcodes.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10);
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO t VALUES (1, 999);
SELECT id, v FROM t ORDER BY id;

cases.name: or-ignore-partial-multirow
cases.description: In a multi-row INSERT OR IGNORE, conflicting tuples are skipped; non-conflicting ones succeed.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (2, 20);
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO t VALUES (1, 10), (2, 99), (3, 30);
SELECT id, v FROM t ORDER BY id;
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10);
INSERT OR REPLACE INTO t VALUES (1, 999);
SELECT id, v FROM t ORDER BY id;
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10), (2, 20);
INSERT OR REPLACE INTO t VALUES (2, 888), (3, 30);
SELECT id, v FROM t ORDER BY id;

cases.name: default-insert-still-conflicts
cases.description: Without OR IGNORE/REPLACE, duplicate key still raises STORAGE_UNIQUE_VIOLATION (phase 9g behavior preserved).

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 20);

cases.name: or-ignore-on-unique-index
cases.description: OR IGNORE also skips conflicts on a non-PK UNIQUE index (9g path).

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_email ON t (email);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'a@x');
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO t VALUES (2, 'a@x');
SELECT id, email FROM t ORDER BY id;

cases.name: or-replace-on-unique-index
cases.description: OR REPLACE on non-PK UNIQUE: DELETEs the old row that holds the conflicting key, then INSERTs the new row.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_email ON t (email);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'a@x');
INSERT OR REPLACE INTO t VALUES (2, 'a@x');
SELECT id, email FROM t ORDER BY id;
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10), (2, 20), (3, 30);
INSERT OR REPLACE INTO t VALUES (2, 888);
SELECT id, v FROM t ORDER BY id;

cases.name: or-ignore-no-conflict
cases.description: OR IGNORE with no conflict is identical to plain INSERT.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO t VALUES (1, 10);
SELECT id, v FROM t;

cases.name: or-rollback-rejected
cases.description: v1 only supports IGNORE and REPLACE; OR ROLLBACK / OR ABORT / OR FAIL are parse errors.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY);
INSERT OR ROLLBACK INTO t VALUES (1);
